findings.title: The deliverable says the task was not done: no primary source was opened
findings.detail: The claim is that the change correctly and completely implements "verify every k(T) law and citation in geometry/stack.py against primary sources". The note contradicts this on its own first lines. It says "No: the task as written (verify against primary sources) could not be completed. In this session I opened none of Incropera, Slack 1973, Hirosaki 2002, the CRC Handbook, Levinshtein 2001 or a TCAD manual". The INDEX line opens with "PARTIAL, no primary source opened". Every law's status rests on secondary material: Scribd OCR scans, aggregator abstracts, search-engine summaries of an unreadable patent, a carried-over attempt-1 reading, or statements credited to a review in project/reviews/T0157/. That directory does not exist in this repository. Discrepancy rows #2, #4, #7 and #11 are explicitly unverified or not found. The note is honest about this, but honesty does not make the claim of complete primary-source verification true.
findings.evidence: research/notes/o006-kT-citations.md lines 2 and 5 (Answer) and 'Verification limits'; INDEX.md entry; `ls project/reviews` returns 'No such file or directory'.
findings.suggested_check: Close the task as not done (or re-scope it as partial), and get library or founder access to Incropera A.1/A.2, Slack 1973, Hirosaki 2002, Burgemeister 1979, CRC and Qian 2017.

findings.title: The SAC305/tin resistivity coefficient 'correction' mixes reference temperatures; the code's 4.2e-3 /K is already consistent
findings.detail: The note calls the code's alpha = 4.2e-3 /K low, compared with secondary tin values of 4.6-4.7e-3 /K over 0-100 C. It then suggests sweeping 4.2-4.7e-3, and plugs 4.7e-3 straight into the code's formula to get f(480 K) = 0.867. But a 0-100 C coefficient is relative to rho(0 C), while stack.py uses rho(300 K)[1 + alpha (T - 300)]. Converted to the code's reference, alpha_300 = alpha_0 / (1 + alpha_0 x 26.85), which gives 4.09e-3 to 4.17e-3 /K. With that, f(480)/f(300) is 0.914-0.921, and the code (0.911) is already slightly steeper. Engineering Toolbox also lists tin at 4.2e-3 /C relative to 20 C. So discrepancy #6 and its proposed sweep range, which feed the P1 sensitivity ranges, are wrong. The note's claim that 4.7e-3 'moves the formula toward [S11]' rests on the same error.
findings.evidence: Scratch script: a0 = 4.6e-3 gives a(300 K) = 0.00409 and f480 = 0.9211; a0 = 4.7e-3 gives a(300 K) = 0.00417 and f480 = 0.9137; the code with 4.2e-3 gives f480 = 0.9112; the note's 4.7e-3 in the code's form gives 0.8667.
findings.suggested_check: Convert every quoted resistivity coefficient to the code's 300 K reference before comparing; drop or re-derive the 4.2-4.7e-3 sweep.

findings.title: The Si3N4 'too shallow' hint has the sign backwards
findings.detail: The note quotes a source saying some Si3N4 grades lose up to 45 % of k between 0 and 400 C. It calls this 'a weakly sourced hint that -1.0 may be too shallow for some grades'. A 1/T law loses 59 % over 273-673 K (ratio 0.406). A loss of at most 45 % corresponds to an exponent of about -0.66, so if anything it suggests -1.0 is too steep. Any sweep built on this hint would widen in the wrong direction.
findings.suggested_check: Recompute the implied exponent for every percentage-loss datum before stating a direction.

findings.title: The Burgemeister 1979 exponent was confirmable but is reported as unconfirmed
findings.detail: The note says its search confirmed only the paper's identity, not the T^-1.49 exponent or the roughly 30 % lower conductivity parallel to c. A sciencegate mirror of the abstract states both: purest samples, normal to c, T^-1.49, 3.87 W/(cm K), parallel to c about 30 % lower, 300-500 K. This supports discrepancy #1 (a 6H, normal-to-c exponent applied to 4H along c). But it shows the 'could not verify' status is partly an incomplete search, not a hard access limit.
findings.suggested_check: Cite the abstract mirror for the exponent and the c-axis anisotropy.

findings.title: The Ioffe T-fit is compared with the 4H value, but its figure is labelled 6H
findings.detail: The note compares 611/(T-115) (3.30 W/(cm K) at 300 K) with the 4H value of 3.7 and concludes the fit 'does not reproduce 3.7'. The Ioffe figure caption for that fit says 6H-SiC monocrystalline, so the comparison mixes polytypes.
findings.evidence: WebSearch summary of ioffe.ru SiC thermal page; 611/185 = 3.303.
findings.suggested_check: State the polytype of the Nilsson fit, or drop the comparison.

findings.title: Breaks mf-research note rules (citing unopened sources, Answer length, provenance header)
findings.detail: mf-research says 'Never cite a source you did not open'. S2 and S6 are bibliographic records only, S5 is abstract-only with 'numbers not read', and S11 is a summary of a scan that could not be read. All four are still cited for content. The Answer runs well past 5 sentences. The header names Task T0157, attempt 2, while this review is for T0175. Several key statements are credited to a review file that is not in the repo, so they cannot be traced from this commit.
findings.suggested_check: Keep unread items in Open questions rather than Sources, and fix the task id.

independent_checks_performed: Read stack.py lines 1-125 and listed every k(T) law and citation (Cu/Incropera A.1, Al2O3/Incropera A.2, Slack 1973, Hirosaki 2002, SAC305 Wiedemann-Franz plus CRC tin coefficient, 4H-SiC Levinshtein/TCAD, datasheet values). Checked them against the note's coverage: the citations are listed, but several are marked unchecked or not found.

Recomputed every number in the note with K_LAWS imported from the repo. Cu slope -1.995e-4 and the 12.5 % shallower 400-600 K slope; Al2O3 exponents -1.0781 and -1.2661; SAC305 f(423)/f(300) = 0.9297 and f(480)/f(300) = 0.9112; Wiedemann-Franz estimate 56.3 W/(m K); 1.6^-1.49 = 0.4964 and 1.6^-1.26 = 0.5531 (the note writes 0.5530); 611/185 = 3.30. All match except trivial rounding.

Converted the 0-100 C tin coefficients (4.6-4.7e-3) to the code's 300 K reference: 4.09-4.17e-3, f(480) = 0.914-0.921. This shows the note's 'alpha appears low' correction is a reference-temperature error.
Computed the exponent implied by the quoted 'up to 45 % loss, 0-400 C' Si3N4 datum: -0.66. It is shallower than -1.0, which reverses the note's inference.
WebSearch for the Burgemeister 1979 abstract: the sciencegate mirror confirms T^-1.49, normal to c, 3.87 W/(cm K), parallel to c about 30 % lower, 6H, 300-500 K.
WebSearch for 10.1063/1.4790134: confirms the measurement is normal to the c axis and gives T^-1.26 for N-type 4H; 280 W/(m K) not confirmed.
WebFetch of arXiv 1712.00830 abstract: confirms TDTR, 250-450 K, in-plane and cross-plane for n-type 4H, SI 4H and SI 6H; no numbers in the abstract.

WebSearch for the Hirosaki 2002 abstract: confirms Green-Kubo MD on ideal crystals and the 300 K values; the T-exponent is not available. WebFetch of the MRS-J PDF returned only a JBIG2 scan, matching the note's access limit.
WebSearch for the Ioffe SiC page (direct fetch failed TLS for me too): 4H = 3.7 W/(cm K); the 611/(T-115) fit's figure is labelled 6H.
WebSearch for tin coefficient tables: Engineering Toolbox gives 4.2e-3 relative to 20 C; others give 4.5e-3.
Checked the repository for the cited review file: project/reviews/ does not exist at this commit. The diff touches only the note and one INDEX line.
caveats: The deliverable file exists and is candid about its limits. If the task were re-scoped to 'a partial, secondary-source audit of the k(T) citations', its main SiC finding would mostly stand: a 6H, normal-to-c exponent applied to a 4H die whose heat flows along c, which I confirmed via an abstract mirror. So would its Cu/Al2O3 number checks and its Hirosaki point (ideal-crystal MD).
I could not open the primary documents either (Incropera, Slack, Hirosaki full text, CRC, Qian 2017, Levinshtein). My checks are arithmetic plus secondary or abstract sources.
As the note says, E006 pass/fail compares against references that use the same k(T) laws, so these citation issues bear on the P1 pilot sensitivity ranges, not on E006.
